title: Session Credit Fold — compact token-level attribution & export UX
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers need a compact way to inspect per-session spend (token credits consumed across multiple model variants and fallbacks) inside the Redwood Console without losing context. Large tabular exports and token-heavy breakdowns overwhelm product managers and billing teams when investigating anomalous charges.

Goal: Design a compact, exportable UI pattern — the 'Session Credit Fold' — that surfaces per-session token consumption, attribution across routes and model variants, and a frictionless CSV and JSON export flow. The view must fit inside existing Console dashboards as an expandable panel and also work standalone as an export-first artifact for finance and SRE teams.

Scope:
- Compact row-first UI for session-level summaries with expandable per-message token lines.
- Attribution badges showing route, model-variant, and inferred prompt-template.
- Quick-filters (time window, customer segment, SLA tier) and lightweight sparklines.
- Export target presets: CSV (compact line format), JSON (full lineage), and Audit-Ready CSV (includes signer/metadata).
- Accessibility-focused controls: keyboard expandable rows, screen-reader labels for expansion state.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Trade-off between showing full KV/cache hit/miss detail vs. keeping rows scannable. We expose hits/misses in the expanded detail only to minimize noise.
- To avoid overloading the console, heavy lineage (full token-by-token trace) is gated behind a 'Download full lineage' flow that streams into a background job.
- Pricing display sticks to unit-cost bands (per-token effective cost) instead of raw cents to reduce cognitive load; finance export includes raw cents per line.

Outcome: Deliver Figma components, annotated export schema, acceptance criteria, and a short usability script for a 5-person internal validation session.
acceptance_criteria: Session Credit Fold component implemented in Figma with expand/collapse states and keyboard interactions
Panel integrated into Dashboard as an expandable card; shows aggregated per-session spend and per-message lines on expand
Export presets available in UI: Compact CSV, Full Lineage JSON, Audit-Ready CSV; each map to documented schema in Confluence
Usability test with 5 internal participants yields no major usability blockers (<=2 critical issues)
Design handoff includes annotated tokens for accessibility and a redlines spec for dev (colors, spacing, responsive breakpoints)
comments: 2025-02-14 - Ava Chen: Initial concept walkthrough with PM and Eng. PM asked to prioritize 'Audit-Ready' export for enterprise customers with KMS metadata. Eng flagged background export job requirement (ENG-7801) to avoid UI timeouts.
2025-02-17 - Priya Kapoor: Implemented three micro-ux variants (compact, stacked, chip-list) in Figma. Chose 'compact row-first' after quick heuristic test — better scan speed for finance use-cases.
2025-02-19 - Diego (Eng lead): Reviewed API contract for export presets; requested inclusion of model-variant hash and routing-policy id to connect with Serve logs. Added as dependency ENG-7801.

2025-02-21 - Accessibility review (Liam O'Connor): Recommended explicit aria-expanded states and larger hit-targets for expand chevrons. Also suggested color-blind safe palette for attribution badges.
2025-02-24 - PM review (Nina Park): Asked for quick filter defaults to be 'last 7 days' and 'only billed sessions' to reduce noise for first-time users. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-26 - Design critique: Risk noted: compacting too much may hide cache hit patterns that SREs need. Decision: add a single-line 'cache-hit ratio' sparkline on collapsed rows and full KV table in expanded view.
2025-02-28 - Priya Kapoor: Submitted final Figma file and annotated export schema to Confluence. Ready for dev handoff; segue ticket PM-4299 created for rollout plan.
